subject: Fit model with one error term on original scale and one on log scale

messages.author: ef8463d2fe864477
messages.subject: Fit model with one error term on original scale and one on log scale
parts:
Is it possible to fit a model with an error term on original scale (eps_I) and one on log scale (eps) with INLA? And how is such a model specified with the call to the inla function of RInla?

y = eta + eps_N
log(eta) = X beta + eps
eps_N ~ N(0,tau_N)
eps ~ N(0, tau)

Background:
I want to analyze data with a stochastic component at log-scale, i.e. lognormal, but measurement error on original scale is assumed normal.
In the studied soil CO2 efflux data, total error increases with response magnitude, but there are scatter and negative observations for small responses.
I want to disentangle the two sources.

In the real data the "X beta" part is more complex involves a smoother with time and random effects by location that also slowly change with time. This is hard to explore with MCMC and I hoped I could use INLA.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fit model with one error term on original scale and one on log scale
parts:
Hi,

Yes, this should be possible, at least in the type of structure you describe, where the log-link applies to the whole linear predictor except for the final Gaussian error term. You will need to tell inla to use a log-link with the Gaussian observation family instead of the default identity-link. You can think of the observation model as being

Y~ N(exp(eta), tau_N)
where eta is the linear model
eta=X beta + eps

(In INLA terminology, eta is always the linear predictor)

(For more complex nonlinear constructions the inlabru package allows more general predictor expressions, but in your case plain inla should be fine)

Finn

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fit model with one error term on original scale and one on log scale
parts:
n = 300
x1 = rnorm(n, sd=0.2)
x2 = rnorm(n, sd=0.2)
eps = rnorm(n, sd = 0.1)
eta = x1 + x2 + eps
y = exp(eta) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.1)

r = inla(y ~ -1 + x1 + x2 + f(idx),
data = data.frame(y, x1, x2, idx = 1:n),
control.family = list(
control.link = list(
model = "log")))
summary(r)
